title: Matthew Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 7.

questions.question: In Matthew 7, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Judge not, that ye be not judged.
Ask, and it shall be given you;
Give not that which is holy unto the dogs,
Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye;
questions.correctAnswer: Judge not, that ye be not judged.
questions.explanation: This is the very first statement in Matthew 7:1, establishing a key teaching about judgment.

questions.question: According to Matthew 7, what will happen with the judgment we give?
options: It shall be measured to you again.
We will be rewarded for it.
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be measured to you again.
questions.explanation: This is directly stated in Matthew 7:2, indicating the reciprocal nature of judgment.

questions.question: What metaphor does Matthew 7:3 use to illustrate the issue of judgment?
options: The mote in a brother's eye
The stone given to a son
The beam in one's own eye
questions.correctAnswer: The mote in a brother's eye
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:3 discusses the mote in a brother's eye as a metaphor for focusing on others' faults while ignoring our own.

questions.question: What does Matthew 7:5 say should be done first before addressing another's fault?
options: Cast out the beam out of thine own eye
Ask and it shall be given
questions.correctAnswer: Cast out the beam out of thine own eye
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:5 instructs that one must first remove their own faults before addressing those of others.

questions.question: In Matthew 7:6, what should not be given to the dogs?
questions.correctAnswer: That which is holy
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:6 explicitly states not to give what is holy to dogs, emphasizing the value of sacred things.

questions.question: What promise is found in Matthew 7:7 regarding asking?
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be given you
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:7 assures that asking will result in receiving, highlighting the positive outcome of seeking.

questions.question: Who receives when they ask according to Matthew 7:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Every one that asketh
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:8 states that everyone who asks receives, emphasizing the inclusivity of this promise.

questions.question: What does Matthew 7:9 compare a father's response to a son's request for bread?
options: Will he give him a stone?
Will he give him a serpent?
questions.correctAnswer: Will he give him a stone?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 7:9, the question posed is whether a father would give a stone instead of bread, illustrating the nature of good gifts.

questions.question: What does Matthew 7:10 ask about a father's response to a request for fish?
options: Will he give him a serpent?
Will he give him a rock?
Will he give him a chicken?
questions.correctAnswer: Will he give him a serpent?
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:10 raises the question of whether a father would give a serpent instead of a fish, further emphasizing the idea of good gifts.

questions.question: According to Matthew 7, if you judge others, what can you expect?
questions.correctAnswer: You will be judged
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:2 clearly states that with the same judgment you use, you will be judged, indicating a reciprocal effect.

questions.question: In Matthew 7, what should be removed first according to Jesus?
questions.correctAnswer: Beam from your own eye
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:5 instructs to first remove the beam from your own eye before addressing others' faults.

questions.question: True or False: Matthew 7:1 says that we should judge others.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:1 explicitly states, 'Judge not, that ye be not judged,' indicating we should not judge others.

questions.question: True or False: Matthew 7:8 states that everyone who seeks will find.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:8 confirms that everyone who seeks will find, highlighting the promise given to those who search.

questions.question: True or False: According to Matthew 7:6, we should cast our pearls before swine.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:6 warns against casting pearls before swine, indicating this is not something we should do.

questions.question: True or False: In Matthew 7:10, a father is said to give his son a serpent when he asks for fish.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:10 asks if a father would give a serpent instead of fish, implying he would not, thus making this statement false.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Matthew 7:11, how does the Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him?
options: He gives good things because He is just
He gives good things as He pleases
He gives good things because people are evil
questions.correctAnswer: He gives good things abundantly
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:11 explains that if even evil people know how to give good gifts to their children, then how much more will the Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him.

questions.question: What does Matthew 7:12 promise will happen if someone does what verse 7 commands?
options: They will find what they seek
They will be judged less harshly
They will enter the kingdom of heaven
questions.correctAnswer: They will find what they seek
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:7 commands to ask, seek, and knock, and Matthew 7:8 promises that everyone who seeks will find, connecting the command to the promised outcome.

questions.question: What is the 'law and the prophets' summarized as in Matthew 7?
options: Do unto others as you would have them do unto you
questions.correctAnswer: Do unto others as you would have them do unto you
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:12 states that doing to others as you would have them do to you is the law and the prophets summarized.

questions.question: How do Matthew 7:15 and Matthew 7:20 connect in teaching about false prophets?
options: False prophets are known by their fruits
False prophets teach only the law
False prophets are welcomed by many
questions.correctAnswer: False prophets are known by their fruits
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:15 warns about false prophets in sheep’s clothing, and Matthew 7:20 teaches that by their fruits you shall know them, linking their behavior to identifying them.

questions.question: What practical lesson does Matthew 7:13 teach about the gate and the way?
options: Enter through the narrow gate to find life
Choose the broad way for ease
questions.correctAnswer: Enter through the narrow gate to find life
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:13 instructs to enter the narrow gate, contrasting it with the wide gate leading to destruction, emphasizing the importance of choosing the right path.

questions.question: According to Matthew 7:14, what characterizes the way that leads to life?
options: It is narrow and few find it
questions.correctAnswer: It is narrow and few find it
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:14 describes the way to life as narrow and that few find it, highlighting the challenge of living rightly.

questions.question: What warning does Matthew 7:15 give about false prophets?
options: They come in sheep’s clothing but are inwardly ravening wolves
They preach only the Old Testament
questions.correctAnswer: They come in sheep’s clothing but are inwardly ravening wolves
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:15 warns that false prophets appear harmless like sheep but inwardly are dangerous like ravening wolves.

questions.question: How can you identify false prophets according to Matthew 7:16?
questions.correctAnswer: By their fruits
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:16 teaches that you shall know false prophets by their fruits, just as you cannot gather grapes from thorns.

questions.question: What does Matthew 7:17 say about good and corrupt trees?
options: Good trees bring forth good fruit; corrupt trees bring forth evil fruit
Good trees sometimes produce bad fruit
Corrupt trees can produce good fruit occasionally
Trees do not matter for fruit quality
questions.correctAnswer: Good trees bring forth good fruit; corrupt trees bring forth evil fruit
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:17 explains that good trees produce good fruit and corrupt trees produce evil fruit, illustrating the nature of people by their actions.

questions.question: What does Matthew 7:18 say about the possibility of a good tree producing evil fruit?
options: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit
A good tree sometimes produces evil fruit
A good tree and evil fruit are unrelated
A good tree produces both good and evil fruit
questions.correctAnswer: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:18 states that a good tree cannot produce evil fruit, reinforcing the consistency between nature and behavior.

questions.question: According to Matthew 7:19, what happens to every tree that does not bring forth good fruit?
options: It is hewn down and cast into the fire
It is pruned and cared for
It is left to grow wild
questions.correctAnswer: It is hewn down and cast into the fire
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:19 warns that trees that do not produce good fruit are cut down and thrown into the fire, symbolizing judgment.

questions.question: How does Matthew 7:20 summarize the way to recognize false teachers?
questions.correctAnswer: By their fruits
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:20 concludes that false teachers are known by their fruits, meaning their actions and outcomes reveal their true nature.

questions.question: True or False: Matthew 7:1 commands believers to judge others so they will not be judged themselves.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:1 instructs believers not to judge others so that they themselves will not be judged.

questions.question: True or False: Matthew 7:5 advises first to remove the beam from your own eye before helping remove the mote from your brother’s eye.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:5 teaches that one must first remove the beam from their own eye to see clearly to help remove the mote from another’s eye.

questions.question: True or False: Matthew 7:6 encourages believers to give what is holy to dogs and cast pearls before swine.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:6 warns against giving what is holy to dogs or casting pearls before swine, to prevent them from trampling and attacking.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 7.

questions.question: According to Matthew 7:21, who shall enter into the kingdom of heaven?
options: He that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven
Every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord
Those who prophesy in my name
Those who cast out devils in my name
questions.correctAnswer: He that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:21 states that not everyone who calls Jesus 'Lord' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only those who do the will of the Father in heaven.

questions.question: In Matthew 7:22, what do many claim to have done in Jesus' name?
options: Prophesied, cast out devils, and done many wonderful works
Sought and found the kingdom of heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Prophesied, cast out devils, and done many wonderful works
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:22 records many saying they have prophesied, cast out devils, and done many wonderful works in Jesus' name.

questions.question: What does Jesus say to those who say 'Lord, Lord' but work iniquity, according to Matthew 7:23?
options: I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity
Enter into the kingdom of heaven
You shall be justified on the last day
questions.correctAnswer: I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:23 records Jesus declaring He never knew those who work iniquity and telling them to depart from Him.

questions.question: In the parable of the wise and foolish builders in Matthew 7:24-27, what is the foundation of the wise man's house?
questions.correctAnswer: A rock
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:24 says the wise man built his house upon a rock, making it withstand storms.

questions.question: According to Matthew 7:25, what natural elements beat upon the house built on the rock?
questions.correctAnswer: Rain, floods, and winds
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:25 describes rain descending, floods coming, and winds blowing and beating upon the house built on the rock.

questions.question: What is the result for the house built upon the sand as described in Matthew 7:27?
options: It fell, and great was the fall of it
It stood firm against the storms
It was rebuilt upon the rock
questions.correctAnswer: It fell, and great was the fall of it
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:27 says the house built upon the sand fell when the rains and winds came, and the fall was great.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ἐπιγινώσκω' (epiginōskō) in Matthew 7:23 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To know fully or acknowledge
questions.explanation: In Matthew 7:23, 'I never knew you' uses 'ἐπιγινώσκω,' meaning to know fully or acknowledge someone personally.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Matthew 7:24-27 with the two houses built on different foundations?
questions.correctAnswer: Parable
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:24-27 uses a parable contrasting two builders to teach about obedience and stability.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed by Matthew 7:21’s emphasis on doing God's will?
options: Psalm 40:8 - 'I delight to do thy will, O my God'
Genesis 1:1 - 'In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth'
Exodus 20:3 - 'Thou shalt have no other gods before me'
Isaiah 53:5 - 'He was wounded for our transgressions'
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 40:8 - 'I delight to do thy will, O my God'
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:21’s focus on doing the Father’s will echoes Psalm 40:8, expressing delight in God’s will.

questions.question: Matthew 7:15 warns about false prophets. Which New Testament passage similarly warns about false teachers by their fruits?
options: Romans 12:2 - 'Be not conformed to this world'
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Peter 2:1 - 'False teachers among you'
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:1 also warns of false teachers who bring destructive heresies, echoing Matthew 7:15’s caution against false prophets.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Matthew 7:21 in the chapter?
options: Verse 20, which says 'Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them'
Verse 24, about the wise man building his house
questions.correctAnswer: Verse 20, which says 'Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them'
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:20 precedes 7:21 and emphasizes knowing people by their fruits, setting context for Jesus’ teaching about true discipleship.

questions.question: The contrast between the wise and foolish builders in Matthew 7:24-27 is an example of which typology?
options: Typology of obedience as foundation for spiritual stability
Typology of Israel and the Gentiles
Typology of the law and grace
questions.correctAnswer: Typology of obedience as foundation for spiritual stability
questions.explanation: The parable typifies obedience to Jesus’ words as the foundation for life’s enduring stability (Matthew 7:24-27).

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophecy about knowing God is inversely reflected in Matthew 7:23's 'I never knew you'?
options: Hosea 6:6 - 'I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings'
Jeremiah 31:33 - 'I will put my law in their inward parts'
Micah 6:8 - 'What doth the LORD require of thee?'
questions.correctAnswer: Hosea 6:6 - 'I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings'
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:23's rejection 'I never knew you' contrasts with Hosea 6:6's emphasis on the knowledge of God being paramount.

questions.question: Matthew 7:28-29 highlight the people's reaction to Jesus' teaching. What authority is contrasted with that of the scribes here?
options: Jesus taught as one having authority
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus taught as one having authority
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:29 contrasts Jesus' authoritative teaching with the scribes' less authoritative style.

questions.question: True or False: Matthew 7:24 says the wise man built his house upon the sand.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:24 clearly states the wise man built his house upon a rock, not sand.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 7:1 teach about human sin?
options: Believers must refrain from judging others to avoid divine judgment on themselves
All sin is forgiven without condition
Human judgment is infallible when done righteously
Judgment is reserved only for God and never for humans
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must refrain from judging others to avoid divine judgment on themselves
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:1 teaches that judgment of others results in being judged oneself, emphasizing the doctrine of humility and self-examination in relation to human sin.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 7:6 teach about sanctification?
options: The holy should not be given to those who will profane it
All people should receive the gospel regardless of response
Sanctification is achieved through ritual purity
Believers must share everything equally without distinction
questions.correctAnswer: The holy should not be given to those who will profane it
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:6 teaches that that which is holy should not be given to 'dogs' or 'swine,' illustrating the doctrine of protecting sacred things from profanation as part of sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 7:21 teach about salvation?
options: Not everyone who calls Jesus 'Lord' will enter the kingdom, but only those who do the Father's will
Faith alone without works guarantees entrance into the kingdom
Salvation is given based on lineage and heritage
Public confession is sufficient for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Not everyone who calls Jesus 'Lord' will enter the kingdom, but only those who do the Father's will
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:21 stresses that doing the will of the Father is necessary for entering the kingdom, highlighting the doctrine that true salvation involves obedience, not mere profession.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 7:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:11 demonstrates God's providence in giving good gifts to those who ask, reflecting His caring and sustaining nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 7:29 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Authority
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:29 shows Jesus teaching with authority unlike the scribes, revealing the divine attribute of authoritative teaching and sovereignty.

questions.question: How does Matthew 7:13 connect to broader biblical themes about salvation?
options: It corresponds with the theme of narrow path leading to life found in Luke 13:24
It contradicts the universal invitation of salvation in Acts 2
It denies the need for repentance emphasized in Ezekiel
questions.correctAnswer: It corresponds with the theme of narrow path leading to life found in Luke 13:24
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:13’s teaching about the narrow gate aligns with Luke 13:24’s emphasis on striving to enter the narrow door, reflecting consistent biblical teaching on salvation.

questions.question: How does Matthew 7:15 prepare for New Testament warnings about false teachers?
options: It anticipates Pauline warnings about false apostles in 2 Corinthians
It endorses all religious teachers without discernment
It denies the existence of spiritual deception
It promotes tolerance of false doctrine
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates Pauline warnings about false apostles in 2 Corinthians
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:15 warns about false prophets in sheep's clothing, paralleling Paul's warnings about false apostles in 2 Corinthians, thus preparing for ongoing New Testament concern with doctrinal purity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Matthew 7:3 and Matthew 7:5 teach about human sin and sanctification?
options: Self-examination and repentance are prerequisites for helping others in their sin
Judging others is encouraged without self-reflection
Sanctification depends solely on external works
Hypocrisy is a virtue in community
questions.correctAnswer: Self-examination and repentance are prerequisites for helping others in their sin
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:3 and 7:5 teach that one must first remove the 'beam' from one’s own eye before helping a brother with a 'mote,' emphasizing introspection and repentance before aiding others.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 7:16 and Matthew 7:20 teach about true discipleship?
options: True discipleship is discerned by the fruits or works produced
questions.correctAnswer: True discipleship is discerned by the fruits or works produced
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:16 and 7:20 show that true disciples are known by their fruits, teaching that authentic faith manifests in godly works.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 7:24 and Matthew 7:27 teach about obedience and judgment?
options: Obedience to Jesus’ sayings results in stability at final judgment, while disobedience leads to ruin
Faith alone without obedience guarantees security
Judgment is arbitrary and unrelated to conduct
Hearing alone without doing is sufficient for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to Jesus’ sayings results in stability at final judgment, while disobedience leads to ruin
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:24 and 7:27 use the metaphor of wise and foolish builders to teach that hearing and doing Jesus’ words leads to security, while neglect brings destruction, linking obedience and judgment.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Matthew 7:7-11 teaches that God gives everything asked for unconditionally. What does Matthew 7:7-11 actually teach?
options: God gives good gifts to those who ask according to His will, not all requests unconditionally
God grants every request regardless of its nature
The passage teaches that asking is unnecessary because God knows needs
Prayer has no effect on God’s decisions
questions.correctAnswer: God gives good gifts to those who ask according to His will, not all requests unconditionally
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:7-11 shows that God, as a good Father, gives good gifts to those who ask, implying alignment with His will and goodness rather than unconditional granting of all requests.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 7:22 teach about false profession of faith?
options: External miracles and works do not guarantee acceptance by Christ
Public confession is the only requirement for acceptance
questions.correctAnswer: External miracles and works do not guarantee acceptance by Christ
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:22 shows many will claim miraculous works in Jesus’ name but still be rejected, teaching that external works apart from obedience do not assure salvation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 7:17 and Matthew 7:18 teach about human nature and spiritual fruitfulness?
options: A corrupt nature produces evil fruit; a good nature produces good fruit
Human nature is neutral and can produce any fruit
Good fruit can come from corrupt hearts
Fruitfulness is independent of the inner nature
questions.correctAnswer: A corrupt nature produces evil fruit; a good nature produces good fruit
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:17 and 7:18 teach that the nature of the tree determines the quality of its fruit, illustrating the biblical doctrine that inner spiritual condition affects outward conduct.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 7:2 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:2 teaches that the measure one uses will be measured back to them, reflecting God's justice in reciprocal judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 7:23 teach about relationship with Christ and works?
options: True relationship with Christ is known by Him and evidenced by righteousness, not just works
Works alone secure a saving relationship
Relationship with Christ is guaranteed by public ministry
Faith is irrelevant if works are done
questions.correctAnswer: True relationship with Christ is known by Him and evidenced by righteousness, not just works
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:23 shows Jesus rejecting those who have done works but are unknown to Him, teaching that saving relationship requires His recognition and a life free from iniquity.
